name: Ertapenem
executiveSummary: Once-daily carbapenem. Adult **1 g IV/IM every 24 h**. Pediatrics 3 months–12 years: **15 mg/kg every 12 h** (max **1 g/day**); ≥13 years: **1 g/day**. No anti-Pseudomonas activity.
indications:
## Indications

- Complicated intra-abdominal infection, complicated UTI/pyelonephritis, skin/soft tissue, community-acquired pneumonia, colorectal prophylaxis (regimens).
- Useful for OPAT / step-down because of once-daily dosing.

## Precautions

- **Does not cover Pseudomonas or Acinetobacter**.
- Adjust in renal failure. Seizure risk (lower than imipenem) with CNS disease/renal failure.
- IM only with 1% lidocaine (no epinephrine); do not give that solvent IV.

> Prefer NS dilution; avoid D5W because of instability.

adulto.dose: **1 g IV or IM every 24 h**. Usual duration 5–14 days by site. Renal: CrCl ≤30 mL/min **0.5 g every 24 h** (per label).
adulto.administration: IV: reconstitute with 10 mL SW/NS → dilute in 50–100 mL NS; infuse **30 min**. IM: 3.2 mL 1% lidocaine without epinephrine; deep IM within 1 h of reconstitution.
adulto.notes: Max 6 h from reconstitution to end of IV infusion. ~137 mg Na+/g.

pediatrico.dose: 3 months–12 years: **15 mg/kg every 12 h** (max **1 g/day**). ≥13 years: **1 g every 24 h**.
pediatrico.administration: IV 30 min (~20 mg/mL in NS) or IM as adult.
pediatrico.notes: Caution with seizure history or brain injury.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: use promptly (~1 h refrigerated in vial).
- Diluted in NS: ~6 h refrigerated (check product insert).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, diarrhea, headache, phlebitis, vaginitis, seizures (rare), *C. difficile*, IM site pain.
